entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gaius Licinius Macer Calvus was an orator and poet of ancient Rome who rose to prominence in the late Republic era. Born around 60 BC, he became known for his eloquence and rhetorical skills, which earned him a place among the prominent orators of his time. His work includes several speeches and poems that have been preserved in historical texts.

As a leading figure of the Roman oratory tradition, Calvus's influence extended beyond his own works to shape the literary and intellectual landscape of ancient Rome. His legacy can be seen in the many orators who followed him, including Cicero and Ovid. The impact of Calvus's work on later Roman literature and culture is still studied by scholars today.

Despite his significant contributions to Roman oratory, Calvus's own life remains somewhat enigmatic. Little is known about his personal relationships, political affiliations, or eventual fate. However, it is clear that he played a major role in the intellectual and cultural developments of ancient Rome during the late Republic era.
